# Lab 16.9: Column & Row-level Security in BigQuery

## What We Are Going to Do
Hide a sensitive column with a policy tag, and show each user only the rows for their country with a row access policy.

## Steps

1. **Create a sample table.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq mk --dataset --location=US $PROJECT_ID:secure_bq
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false '
CREATE TABLE secure_bq.customers AS
SELECT "Asha" AS name, "US" AS country, "4111111111111111" AS card UNION ALL
SELECT "Ravi", "IN", "5555555555554444" UNION ALL
SELECT "Mia", "US", "378282246310005"'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **Give Alice basic read access.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq add-iam-policy-binding --member=user:alice@YOUR_DOMAIN \
  --role=roles/bigquery.dataViewer $PROJECT_ID:secure_bq.customers
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID \
  --member=user:alice@YOUR_DOMAIN --role=roles/bigquery.jobUser</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **Create a policy tag.** In the console go to **BigQuery → Policy tags** (part of Dataplex Universal Catalog). Create a taxonomy `pii` in location **us** with a tag `card_number`. Turn on **Enforce access control**.

4. **Attach the tag to the column.** Open the `customers` table, click **Edit schema**, select the `card` column, click **Add policy tag**, and choose `card_number`. Save.

5. **Test column security.** As Alice:
   - `SELECT name, country FROM secure_bq.customers` works
   - `SELECT * FROM secure_bq.customers` fails on the `card` column

   Grant **Fine-Grained Reader** on the tag only to people who need card numbers.

6. **Add a row access policy.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false '
CREATE ROW ACCESS POLICY us_only
ON secure_bq.customers
GRANT TO ("user:alice@YOUR_DOMAIN")
FILTER USING (country = "US")'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


7. **Test row security.** As Alice, `SELECT name, country FROM secure_bq.customers` returns only Asha and Mia.

</code></pre>
</div>


   Delete the `pii` taxonomy in **Policy tags**.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Card column | Hidden unless you have Fine-Grained Reader |
| Rows | Filtered by the row access policy |
| Users with no policy match | See no rows once a policy exists |
| Alternative | Dynamic data masking on the same policy tag |
